corpus_definition: To say sorry for something wrong that you did.

forms.definition: words that say you are sorry
forms.example: Please accept my apology.

syn.note: A reason you give for doing something wrong.

forms.definition: to say that you are sorry for something
forms.example: I apologised for being late.

syn.note: Same meaning; everyday phrase.

forms.definition: showing or saying that you are sorry
forms.example: He gave me an apologetic smile.

syn.note: Feeling bad about what you did.

forms.definition: in a way that shows you are sorry
forms.example: She smiled apologetically.

context.text: Rustam forgot his friend's birthday, so he apologised the next day. His friend accepted the apology with a smile.

corpus_definition: To tell someone you are sorry for a mistake.
usage_note: Pattern: apologise to + person + for + noun or -ing: "I apologised to my mum for breaking the cup." American English: apologize.

context.text: Aziz apologised to his teacher for coming late. Then he apologised to the class for the noise.

reviewer_note: Preposition pattern (to person, for thing) shown.

corpus_definition: a formal request to join a school or get a new job

forms.definition: a written request for a job, place at school or similar
forms.example: I sent my application to the university.

syn.note: Asking for something, often formally.
The paper you fill in to ask for something.

forms.definition: a computer program, especially on a phone
forms.example: I downloaded a new app.
forms.note: Short for application = computer program, not a formal request.

forms.definition: to ask formally for something, usually in writing
forms.example: She applied for a job at the bank.

syn.note: Ask for something formally.

forms.definition: affecting or right for a situation
forms.example: The rule is not applicable to children.
forms.note: Belongs to apply = be relevant, not asking for a job. Formal.

people.definition: a person who asks formally for a job or a place
people.example: There were fifty applicants for the job.

context.text: Dilfuza wants to apply to Westminster University in Tashkent. She is writing her application this week.

reviewer_note: app and applicable belong to other senses of apply.

corpus_definition: To ask for something in writing, like a job or course.
particle_note: Not separable: apply for + thing ("apply for a visa"); apply to + organisation ("apply to the bank for a loan").

relations.note: Informal British English: ask for something officially.

context.text: My brother wants to apply for a job in Seoul. First he has to apply for a work visa.

reviewer_note: apply for vs apply to noted.

corpus_definition: a person who plans and designs how buildings should be built

forms.definition: a person whose job is to design buildings
forms.example: The architect showed us the plans for the new school.

syn.note: A person who plans how things look; more general.
A person who plans towns or projects.

forms.definition: the design of buildings, or the study of how to design them
forms.example: Bukhara is famous for its old architecture.

forms.definition: connected with the design of buildings
forms.example: The city has many architectural treasures.

forms.definition: in a way connected with building design
forms.example: The old town is architecturally important.

context.text: An architect from Tashkent designed the new museum. She loves old Uzbek architecture and used blue tiles everywhere.

reviewer_note: Two corpus rows (B2, B1) merged; B1 used. Headword is a person noun, so it stays the main noun entry (rule 6).

corpus_definition: relating to the very cold region around the North Pole

forms.definition: the very cold area around the North Pole
forms.example: Polar bears live in the Arctic.

forms.definition: from or like the cold area around the North Pole
forms.example: We had arctic weather last winter.

syn.note: From the areas around the North or South Pole.
Very cold.
Very cold, with ice.

context.text: Scientists study the ice in the Arctic every year. Last January Tashkent had almost arctic temperatures.

reviewer_note: Antarctic is the South Pole, related but not family.

forms.definition: guns and other weapons
forms.example: The country sells arms to its neighbours.
forms.note: Always plural in this sense; "arm" = part of the body is a different word.

syn.note: Same meaning; more common.

forms.definition: a large group of soldiers who fight on land
forms.example: My uncle served in the army.

syn.note: The armed forces of a country.

forms.definition: to give weapons to someone
forms.example: They armed the guards with sticks.

syn.note: Give someone the things they need.

forms.definition: carrying a weapon, especially a gun
forms.example: Two armed police officers stood at the door.

context.text: Armed guards stand outside the bank every day. They check that nobody brings arms inside.

reviewer_note: arm (body) is a different word; arms = weapons is family.

corpus_definition: protective metal clothing worn by soldiers in past times

forms.definition: metal clothes that soldiers wore long ago to protect their bodies
forms.example: The knight wore heavy armor.

syn.note: Something that keeps you safe.
A flat object held to protect the body.

forms.definition: covered with strong metal for protection
forms.example: An armored car carries the money.

syn.note: Bullets cannot go through it.

context.text: In the Samarkand museum you can see the armor of Timur's soldiers. Today banks use armored vans to carry money.

reviewer_note: American spelling headword; British armour noted.

corpus_definition: to take someone to the police station because they broke the law.

forms.definition: the act of the police taking someone away for a crime
forms.example: The police made three arrests.

syn.note: Catching a person, often after a chase.
Keeping someone in a police station; formal.

forms.definition: to take a person to the police station because of a crime
forms.example: The police arrested the thief.

syn.note: Find and stop someone.
Formal: keep someone at the police station.
Informal: take someone to the police station.

context.text: The police arrested two men at the airport. After the arrest, they found stolen phones in their bags.

corpus_definition: To one side or out of the way.
usage_note: Adverb after verbs: "step aside, put money aside". "aside from" = except: "Aside from rice, we need bread."

relations.note: At a distance; out of the way.

context.text: Please step aside and let the old man pass. My sister also puts some money aside every month.
